record.body:
## Rationale

Any agent with a shell can create a check-run with `runner: aff` and `result: pass` through `adaptive-artifacts`; the contract does not restrict the writer. Oracle tests are cheap (median 0.27 s, about 11 min serial across all acceptances), so `aff verdict` can re-run the frozen tests at head, and at base in a temporary worktree, instead of trusting stored runs. Forging a pass then requires changing a test, which the hashes catch.

## Counter-argument

Verifying stored runs against the store at close (the shipped `close-batch-store-verify` repair) costs nothing at verdict time and keeps one authority. Re-execution makes verdicts slow when an oracle is slow or flaky, needs a base worktree per verdict, and a test that depends on the environment can give a different answer than it did when the run was recorded.

payload.alternatives: trust stored runs verified against the store at close; stored runs normally and re-execute only at the phase-end gate
payload.choice: aff verdict re-executes frozen oracle tests at the revision (and base in a temporary worktree); stored runs are an audit log and cache

record.subject: verdict-authority
